content: Chrome Web Store single purpose policy (developer.chrome.com quality-guidelines): 'An extension must have a single purpose that is narrow and easy to understand. Dont create an extension that requires users to accept bundles of unrelated functionality.' Clearly separate functionalities must ship as separate extensions. Violation codes Red Magnesium / Red Copper / Red Lithium / Red Argon map to single-purpose breaches. The dashboard Privacy practices tab has a mandatory free-text 'single purpose' description field that reviewers read. Quality-guidelines-FAQ frames single purpose as either a narrow subject matter OR a narrow browser function, and says the extension must include only features directly related to that purpose and request only permissions necessary to it.
